messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Spike in 5xx for cross-region requests EU->US (eu-west-1 -> us-west-2). 60% of /v1/generate requests returning 502/503 over last 3m. Auto-escalating to #incidents and paging on-call.

pagerduty: Paging: @alex (rotation: infra). Incident priority P1.

alex: saw it. joining. can someone paste the traceroute / route table?

maria: putting call together — conf bridge https://meet.redwood/team-incident/1785123456 

sam: quick note: customer reports from EU Prod (acct: big-retail) complaining about high latency and partial failures. Looks like routing policy returned weight 100 to us-west-2 for eu-west-1 prefixes.

jin: digging into routing controller now. suspect recent rollout of the "latency-fallback" policy that prunes region pins if cost higher.

alex: if true we need immediate rollback of that rollout to avoid cross-region fanout. Maria, can you patch route policy to enforce region pin for eu-* for 1 hour?

maria: on it. applying conservative pin now. running command:

```
# lock region pins for eu
redwoodctl routing update-policy --name latency-fallback --set region_pin=eu --env prod --override
```

ops-bot: policy update queued. change-id: ch_0a9f2. Expected propagation ~45s.

sam: seeing errors drop a bit — 5xx down to 18% in 30s. still seeing increased p99 latency (1.2s -> 2.6s).

alex: ok good. keep pinning while we validate. Jin, can you check model placement + cache warming for eu region? Might be cold KV cache causing higher latency after pin.

jin: checking pods in eu-west-1. Found a small fleet scaled down after autoscaler bug — desired 30, actual 6 on one AZ (eu-west-1b). Scaling back up now.

```
kubectl scale --replicas=30 deployment/redwood-infer-eu --namespace prod
# watch logs
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=redwood-infer-eu
```

maria: DNS note: AWS Route53 health checks briefly marked eu endpoints as unhealthy due to a bad probe timeout (30s). Health check config unchanged but probes originate from us-west -> causing false negatives.

alex: that explains why route weights shifted. We need two-pronged: (1) maintain region pins (done), (2) re-evaluate healthcheck vantage points and make them eu-aware. Maria, open a follow-up ticket for healthcheck config.

maria: created ticket INF-4723 with details and owner @jin.

cs-team: FYI — I've notified Big Retail CS contact. They reported partial feature degradation; offered workaround to pin region client-side (region header) and provided status link.

sam: rolling counts now look stable. 5xx <= 3% across eu clients. p99 back to ~1.1s after pods scaled and pinning applied.

alex: good. let's keep the patch for 1h and monitor. Jin, please run a canary traffic replay to ensure no regression when we re-enable latency-fallback.

jin: will run replay after warmup. Expected to take ~20m.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial (customer impact reduced). Continue monitoring.

maria: quick postmortem notes: root cause chain: (1) Route53 health check timeouts (from non-local vantage) + (2) new latency-fallback rollout that reweighted traffic to lower-cost region when origin health looked degraded + (3) an autoscaler bug that left eu capacity low in one AZ -> combined to produce cross-region misroutes and elevated 5xx.

alex: action items: INF-4723 (healthcheck eu vantage), INF-4724 (rollback / safe rollout gating for latency-fallback), INF-4725 (autoscaler fix for AZ imbalance), and customer comms draft. Assigning owners: jin -> INF-4723/4725, maria -> INF-4724, cs-team -> customer comm.

sam: recommend adding synthetic probes from eu regions to routing controller, and a circuit-breaker that prevents >10% reroute off-region within 2m.

alex: agreed. add to INF-4724.

pagerduty: Incident annotated: responders acknowledged. Next on-call handoff at 08:00 UTC.

maria: marking incident as "mitigated - monitoring". Will start writeup. Anyone else want to add notes?

cs-team: copied recorded timeline to customer incident page and will follow up after final postmortem. :thumbsup:
